subtitle: When Merchants Carved Their Own Heaven Beside a King’s

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of temple spires against a glowing dusk sky
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho stands in three-quarter view atop a stone plinth, gazing over a clustered skyline of Khajuraho’s temples where one Jain shikhara rises beside towering Shaiva and Vaishnava shrines, fields and village roofs stretching beyond.

dialogue.text: In Chandela Khajuraho, Shaiva kings and Jain merchants raised rival spires side by side—how did one small city carry so many paths without tearing itself apart?

i18n.hi: चंदेला खजुराहो में, शैव राजा और जैन व्यापारी कंधे से कंधा मिलाकर शिखर खड़े कर रहे थे—एक छोटा शहर इतने रास्तों को लेकर भी कैसे न बिखरा?

panels.shot: high bird’s-eye wide over the Khajuraho landscape
panels.action: A panoramic view shows the western temple group with massive Shaiva and Vaishnava shrines on a rise, the eastern group with smaller Jain temples nearer groves and ponds, and a modest town threaded between fields and dusty tracks.

dialogue.text: Around 950 to 1100, Khajuraho was not a ruin in the jungle, but a lived-in Chandela capital, where fields, houses and markets wrapped themselves around stone mountains of gods.

i18n.hi: करीब 950 से 1100 के बीच, खजुराहो जंगल का खंडहर नहीं, जीता-जागता चंदेला राजधानी था, जहाँ खेत, घर और बाज़ार देवों की पत्थर की पहाड़ियों को घेरते थे।

panels.shot: medium wide inside a royal hall
panels.action: A Chandela king sits on a low throne beneath carved beams, priests and court officials at his side, as a temple model of a Shaiva shrine rests before them, artisans and scribes waiting for orders at the edge of the hall.

dialogue.text: Chandela kings poured wealth into Shaiva shrines and allied cults, binding their rule to temple walls; every new mandir on the western hill made their lineage feel taller than stone.

i18n.hi: चंदेला राजाओं ने शैव देवालयों और सहयोगी पंथों पर धन बरसाया, अपनी सत्ता को मंदिरों से बाँध दिया; पश्चिमी पहाड़ी पर हर नया मंदिर उनकी वंशावली को पत्थर से ऊँचा दिखाता।

panels.shot: medium shot in a bustling market street
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho stands in a crowded bazaar lined with stalls of textiles, grain and metalware, weighing coins in his hand as other traders haggle and a Jain monk passes silently in the background.

dialogue.text: Yet in the markets, another power grew—the Jain merchant guilds, whose caravans carried cotton, grain and metal, and whose ledgers could fund whole sanctuaries without a king’s coin.

i18n.hi: पर बाज़ारों में एक और ताकत उगी—जैन व्यापारी संघ, जिनके कारवाँ कपास, अनाज, धातु ढोते, और जिनकी बहीखातें बिना राजा के सिक्के के ही पूरे मंदिर उठा देतीं।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot under a neem tree
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho kneels respectfully before a seated Digambara monk under the shade of a neem tree, while a few traders sit nearby listening, scrolls and donation records neatly rolled beside them.

dialogue.text: Jain mendicants brought more than sermons; they stitched merchants into networks of trust, where vows, endowments and guild decisions turned private wealth into lasting religious institutions.

i18n.hi: जैन साधु सिर्फ उपदेश नहीं लाए; उन्होंने व्यापारियों को भरोसे के जाल में पिरोया, जहाँ व्रत, दान और संघ के फैसले निजी संपत्ति को टिकाऊ धार्मिक संस्थाओं में बदलते गए।

panels.action: Hands of Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho and a stone mason rest on a partly carved block, its surface showing a faint outline of a tirthankara, while in the blurred background a rising temple plinth takes shape among scaffolding.

dialogue.text: By the late tenth century, their resolve hardened into stone: Jain patrons in Khajuraho began commissioning their own shrines, as inscriptions later recorded in fragments at the Ghantai Temple.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के अंत तक, उनकी नीयत पत्थर बन गई: खजुराहो के जैन दानदाताओं ने अपने देवालय बनवाने शुरू किए, जिनका ज़िक्र आगे चलकर घटाई मंदिर की टूटी शिलालेखों में मिला।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of the Ghantai Temple in an earlier intact state
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho walks with an architect beside the newly completed Ghantai Temple, its elegant pillars carved with chain-and-bell motifs and makara arches, the sanctuary entrance aligned toward an inner tirthankara image.

dialogue.text: The Ghantai Temple rose first, its long pillared hall and chain-and-bell carvings proclaiming Digambara Jain devotion; a now-fragmentary inscription noted the merchants behind this quiet architectural statement.

i18n.hi: सबसे पहले उठा घटाई मंदिर, उसका लंबा स्तंभित मंडप और ज़ंजीर-घंटी नक्काशियाँ दिगंबर जैन भक्ति पुकारती रहीं; अब टूटी हुई शिलालेख बताती है, इस शांत स्थापत्य बयान के पीछे कौन से व्यापारी थे।

panels.shot: medium shot at a stone plinth in the Parsvanatha temple
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho traces older reliefs of amorous couples and attendant deities along the outer wall of the Parsvanatha temple, while inside artisans carefully install a serene tirthankara image in the sanctum.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists later saw it clearly: shrines like Parsvanatha and Adinatha reused older Hindu layouts and sculptures, their walls still alive with yakshis and couples, even as their sanctums turned toward Jain tirthankaras.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्वविदों ने बाद में साफ देखा: पार्श्वनाथ और आदिनाथ जैसे देवालय पुराने हिंदू नक्शों और मूर्तियों को ही दोहराते हैं, दीवारों पर यक्षिणियाँ और युगल अब भी नाचते हैं, बस गर्भगृह जैन तीर्थंकरों की ओर मुड़ गया।

panels.shot: three-quarter medium shot of a thoughtful patron in the temple
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho stands between a sensual exterior panel and the calm central tirthankara image, looking from one to the other, his face composed but reflective as lamplight flickers on stone.

dialogue.speaker: jain_merchant_patrons
dialogue.text: Old walls, new vows—we inherit forms, but we choose our centre.

i18n.hi: पुरानी दीवारें, नए व्रत—रूप हम पाते हैं, केंद्र हम चुनते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot showing both western Hindu and eastern Jain temples
panels.action: From a mid-distance vantage, the viewer sees on the left the massive Lakshmana and Kandariya Mahadeva rising with ornate towers, and on the right the smaller but distinct Jain temples clustered among trees, a dusty road linking them.

dialogue.text: Krishna Deva’s careful plans showed how closely the traditions shared space: Chandela-backed Shaiva and Vaishnava giants on the western ridge, merchant-sustained Jain shrines just across fields and tanks to the east.

i18n.hi: कृष्ण देव की सूझबूझ भरी नक्शों ने दिखाया कि परंपराएँ कितनी पास-पास थीं: चंदेला-समर्थित शैव और वैष्णव दैत्य मंदिर पश्चिमी पहाड़ी पर, और व्यापारियों से चलने वाले जैन देवालय खेतों और सरोवरों के पार, ठीक पूरब में।

panels.shot: busy street-level wide between temple groups
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho rides a bullock cart laden with offerings along a road where villagers carrying Shaiva offerings walk one way and Jain householders with lamps and fruit walk the other, all passing each other without incident.

dialogue.text: On certain days, one path led families to Shaiva linga-abhisheka, another to Jain pratikramaṇa; the same streets carried both streams, not from slogans of tolerance, but from habits and agreements that kept business and worship flowing.

i18n.hi: कुछ दिनों में, एक राह परिवारों को शैव लिंग अभिषेक की ओर ले जाती, दूसरी जैन प्रतिक्रमण की ओर; वही गलियाँ दोनों धाराएँ ढोतीं, न नारेबाज़ सहिष्णुता से, बल्कि उन समझौतों से जो व्यापार और पूजा दोनों को बहता रखते थे।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of a council of merchants
panels.action: Inside a simple hall, Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho and other traders sit in a circle with account scrolls, a small chest of coins between them, as they discuss and point toward a sketch of a temple façade on the floor.

dialogue.text: Jain councils decided endowments collectively: who would fund daily rites, who would feed monks, who would pay sculptors. Their corporate giving, traced by scholars like John Cort and Paul Dundas, made stone outlast any one donor.

i18n.hi: जैन परिषदें मिलकर दान तय करतीं: रोज़ की पूजा कौन देगा, साधुओं का भोजन कौन उठाएगा, मूर्तिकारों की मजदूरी कौन भरेगा। जॉन कॉर्ट और पॉल डुंडस जैसे विद्वान जिन कॉर्पोरेट दानों का पीछा करते हैं, उन्होंने पत्थर को किसी एक दानी से लंबा जीने दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a royal audience with merchants
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho stands before the Chandela king in court, offering a modest casket, while the king listens, a priest watching; behind them, a courtier holds a document bearing a sketch of the eastern temple group.

dialogue.text: Chandela rulers allowed these Jain foundations within their sacred capital, for merchants brought revenue and prestige; the king’s own gods remained unshaken, even as other images glowed in neighbouring sanctuaries.

i18n.hi: चंदेला शासकों ने अपनी पवित्र राजधानी में इन जैन संस्थाओं को जगह दी, क्योंकि व्यापारी राजकोष और प्रतिष्ठा दोनों लाते थे; राजा के अपने देव अटल रहे, भले ही पास ही दूसरे मूर्तिचित्र चमक उठे।

panels.shot: twilight wide shot of simultaneous rituals
panels.action: At twilight, in the distance a Shaiva temple courtyard hosts a lamp-lit procession, while closer, within the Jain precinct, Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho joins a quiet tirthankara puja, both rituals visible under the same darkening sky.

dialogue.text: On festival evenings, conch shells could sound from one precinct while the Jain bell chimed from another; Khajuraho’s air carried layered devotions, as if the city itself learned to hold more than one rhythm.

i18n.hi: त्योहार की शामों में, एक प्रांगण से शंख गूँजता, तो दूसरे से जैन घंटा; खजुराहो की हवा परतदार भक्ति से भरती, मानो शहर ने खुद सीख लिया हो कि एक से ज़्यादा ताल कैसे संभाले जाते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on weathered Jain sculptures
panels.action: A present-day view shows worn but still recognizable tirthankara figures and attendant deities on the walls of the Parsvanatha temple, sunlight catching the smoothness of stone polished by centuries of hands.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, many inscriptions fell silent and roofs collapsed, yet the Jain carvings on Parsvanatha, Adinatha and Ghantai still whisper of a time when merchants quietly inscribed their world into the Chandela heartland.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, कई शिलालेख मौन हो गए, छतें गिर पड़ीं, फिर भी पार्श्वनाथ, आदिनाथ और घटाई पर जैन नक्काशियाँ अब भी फुसफुसाती हैं उस वक्त की, जब व्यापारियों ने चुपचाप अपना संसार चंदेला धरती पर उकेर दिया।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of the patron’s face blending into temple stone
panels.action: Jain Merchant Patron of Khajuraho’s calm, aging face fills the frame, then subtly merges with the contours of a tirthankara carving behind him, as if his features dissolve into the stone legacy.

dialogue.text: Khajuraho’s shared skyline did not emerge from pure harmony, nor from constant strife, but from negotiated spaces where a king’s need for legitimacy met a merchant’s wish to honour his own path.

i18n.hi: खजुराहो की साझा क्षितिज रेखा न शुद्ध सौहार्द से बनी, न लगातार टकराव से, बल्कि उन तयशुदा जगहों से जहाँ राजा की वैधता की भूख, व्यापारी की अपने मार्ग को सम्मान देने की चाह से टकराई।

panels.shot: final wide shot of modern visitors walking through both precincts
panels.action: Modern-day visitors wander along paths linking the western and eastern temple groups, some pausing before Hindu shrines, others in the Jain complex, as the same sun lights every tower and path.

dialogue.text: In Khajuraho today, every shared stone between Hindu and Jain shrines recalls a simple lesson: cities grow richer when those who hold power leave room, in their centres, for more than one way to face the sacred.

i18n.hi: आज के खजुराहो में, हिंदू और जैन देवालयों के हर साझा पत्थर एक सीधा सबक दोहराता है: शहर तब अमीर बनते हैं, जब सत्ता पकड़ने वाले अपने केंद्रों में एक से ज़्यादा तरीके से पवित्र की ओर मुड़ने की जगह छोड़ते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Hindu and Jain Builders Share Khajuraho
